mcqs.question: Under Section 187(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, what is the maximum total period of police custody that may be sought in parts during the initial period?
options: 7 days
15 days
40 days
60 days
mcqs.explanation: Police custody may be sought in parts during the initial 40 or 60 days, but the total police custody is capped at 15 days. The periods of 40 and 60 days relate to the window for seeking custody, not the maximum custody itself.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements regarding police custody and related safeguards under the BNSS is incorrect?
options: An accused may meet an advocate during interrogation, but not throughout the interrogation.
A magistrate cannot impose a blanket condition prohibiting any further extension of police custody.
No person may be detained beyond 24 hours without being produced before a magistrate.
Police custody may extend to 30 days in total if it is sought in parts during the initial 40 or 60 days.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that police custody may extend to 30 days. Section 187(2) caps total police custody at 15 days, even when it is sought in parts. The other statements reflect the rules on access to an advocate, magistrate-imposed conditions and detention beyond 24 hours.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Act amends Section 3 of the 1971 Act.
2. Vande Mataram receives the same protection as the National Anthem against intentional prevention or disturbance of singing.
3. The amendment makes singing Vande Mataram compulsory at official gatherings.
options: 1 and 2 only
2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the amendment changes Section 3 and gives Vande Mataram the same protection as the National Anthem against intentional prevention or disturbance of singing. Statement 3 is incorrect because the amendment does not make singing compulsory.

mcqs.question: What punishment is provided under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026, for intentional prevention or disturbance of singing Vande Mataram?
options: Imprisonment up to 1 year only
Imprisonment up to 3 years, fine or both
Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine
Fine only
mcqs.explanation: The punishment is imprisonment up to 3 years, fine or both. A repeat offence under Section 3A carries a minimum of 1 year, but that does not replace the general punishment described here.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The North Eastern Council is established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
Reason (R): The Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Assertion A is false because the North Eastern Council is governed by a separate 1971 Act. Reason R is true because the Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

mcqs.question:
Match the following Zonal Councils with their members:

List-I
 a. Northern Zonal Council
 b. Central Zonal Council
 c. Eastern Zonal Council
 d. Western Zonal Council

List-II
 i. Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
 ii. Goa, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
 iii. Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal and Sikkim
 iv. Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Delhi, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh
options: a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
a-i, b-iv, c-ii, d-iii
a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i
a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iv, b-i, c-iii and d-ii. The Northern, Central, Eastern and Western Zonal Councils respectively comprise the member groups listed in those pairs.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The President assented to the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, which amends the First Schedule.
Statement B: Under Article 3, Parliament can alter the name, area or boundaries of a State, and the State's opinion is not binding.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President assented to the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, amending the First Schedule, while Article 3 empowers Parliament to alter a State's name, area or boundaries and does not make the State's opinion binding.
